=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- changelog.d/7204-force-with-lease-push-rules.md
  Line or code reference: headline bullet, "...and pushes that delete a branch or target `main`/`master` now always ask."
  Problem: The last autofix run added a limitations sentence to the body but left the headline unchanged. The headline still says every branch-deleting push now asks. A colon deletion such as `git push origin claude/x :release` still matches `Bash(git push origin claude/*)` and no `ask` pattern, so it runs without a prompt. The body of the same fragment and CLAUDE.md §21.E say so.
  Why it fails at runtime: Nothing breaks when the code runs. A consumer who reads only the headline, which is what the assembled CHANGELOG surfaces, will believe all branch deletions prompt. CLAUDE.md §20 asks for concrete, verifiable claims. Rewording the headline to "pushes that use `--delete`, `-d` or `--prune`, or name `main`/`master` as a destination, now always ask" would fix it.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

- changelog.d/7204-force-with-lease-push-rules.md
  Line or code reference: Headline bullet (line 2)
  Problem: The headline claims every branch-deleting push now asks for confirmation.
  Why it fails at runtime: Colon-style branch deletions (e.g., git push origin claude/x :release) bypass the ask rules in .claude/settings.json, meaning they proceed unprompted. The headline provides an inaccurate summary of the behavior, misleading the user, even though the body text below it correctly identifies this limitation.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- changelog.d/7204-force-with-lease-push-rules.md
  Line or code reference: line 1 (headline bullet "...and pushes that delete a branch or target `main`/`master` now always ask.")
  Problem: The headline still claims every branch-deleting push now asks, but the body sentence added in this run acknowledges a colon-deletion form such as `git push origin claude/x :release` is not caught: it matches `Bash(git push origin claude/*)` (the trailing `*` swallows `claude/x :release`) and none of the new ask rules match it (they all key on `--delete`, `-d`, or `--prune`). The body now contradicts the headline, and CLAUDE.md §21.E names the colon deletion as a known limitation. The previous AI run documented the limitation in the body but left the headline as-is, so the public-facing claim is still overstated.
  Why it fails at runtime: This is a documentation defect, not a runtime bug. The rules behave exactly as documented in §21.E. But the changelog entry's headline is shipped verbatim into `CHANGELOG.md` by `scripts/assemble_changelog.py` and reaches every consumer on the next `@stable` sync; CLAUDE.md §20.D/E require the headline to name the user-visible change and keep claims "concrete and verifiable." The current claim is not literally true, and a downstream agent that reads only the headline (the §20.D lead paragraph says so) would believe colon-deletion is covered.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
